clue.text: Plump, short, bloated, heartless and wicked

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: plump means fat

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: bloated means bulbous, swollen and rounded

explanation.surface: A string of insults hurled at someone overweight and unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of FAT; 'heartless' removes the middle B of BULBOUS, leaving BULOUS. 'Wicked' is slang praise, not a further insult.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, wicked means excellent or terrific, a synonym of the informal sense of fabulous.

clue.text: It's worth six and two-thirds of 21 roughly

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: roughly means the kept letters are rearranged
two-thirds of means only four of the six letters of that answer are kept, its last four

parts.note: the clue number refers to the answer of 21-down, a networking device

explanation.surface: A puzzling valuation: something is worth six plus a rough fraction of twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' is a cross-reference to 21-down, ROUTER; 'two-thirds of' keeps UTER, and 'roughly' rearranges it to RTUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtue can mean merit or value, as in a plan having the virtue of simplicity, so it matches worth.

clue.text: Good cops beginning to realise nice may be bad

indicators.note: cops in the sense of catches or takes hold of, so the first word grips the rest

parts.note: good in the sense of devout means pious

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged
beginning to means only the first letter of realise is used

explanation.surface: A wry observation that good cop, bad cop has a twist: niceness may turn out to be bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cops' is the verb, catches, not police: the anagram made by 'may be' sits inside the word for good, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernicious means harmful or destructive, a stronger synonym of bad.

clue.text: Business starts to commission orders following expansion

indicators.note: following expansion means the resulting abbreviation is then written out in full
starts to means the first letters of commission and orders are taken

explanation.surface: A firm's growth means it begins taking commissions and orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives CO, the standard abbreviation for the word that 'following expansion' asks the solver to spell out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a commercial firm, so business in the sense of an enterprise is a synonym.

clue.text: Band have a touching relationship with smack

definitions.meaning: An American rock band famed for face paint
in snooker or billiards two balls that touch lightly are said to ...
a smack is a loud ... on the lips

explanation.surface: A band's members are close and affectionate with one another, perhaps too close.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row; the middle one is the billiards sense of balls just touching.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a rock band, the light touch of two balls, and a smacking peck on the cheek.

clue.text: Enacts changes on railway line

indicators.note: changes means the letters of enacts are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes alterations on a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks like part of the railway picture but it is the definition, as in a family line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of descent is one's lineage, the series of forebears that make up a family's heritage.

clue.text: Specialist language almost disappeared following shake up

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: to shake up is to jar or jolt

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: disappeared means gone

explanation.surface: Technical jargon nearly vanished after an organisational shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the specialised vocabulary of a profession or group, hard for outsiders to follow.

clue.text: Ridicule national standard that ignores learning primarily

indicators.note: ignores means a letter is left out

parts.note: the saltire, a white diagonal cross on blue, is the flag of Scotland

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of learning

explanation.surface: Mockery of a national standard of education that neglects learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' is a flag here, not a benchmark: the SALTIRE is Scotland's national flag, St Andrew's cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses humour and exaggeration to mock folly, so it is a form of ridicule.

clue.text: Poor relation from the East

indicators.note: poor means badly formed, so the letters of relation are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor relative who has come from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things of Asia, the lands to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Silence objection to number at university

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student's protest at being reduced to a number at university is shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silence' is a command here: button up is an order to stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To button up is an idiom for keeping quiet, so it works as a command for silence.

clue.text: Butcher mentioned something that goes with reindeer

indicators.note: mentioned means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: to butcher is to slay or slaughter

explanation.surface: A butcher remarks on something associated with reindeer, perhaps venison.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas's reindeer famously pull his sleigh, the sledge that goes with them.

clue.text: Partners drop off to sleep and dribble

indicators.note: drop off means those letters fall away from the word

parts.note: to sleep is to snooze
in bridge, South and North play as partners, giving S and N

explanation.surface: Partners nodding off to sleep and drooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' looks like part of the sleep picture but it signals removal of the bridge partners S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to seep or trickle out slowly, a synonym of dribble.

clue.text: Lead isn't much good at this leading business

definitions.text: Lead isn't much good at this
definitions.meaning: lead the metal is a poor carrier of electricity compared with copper
the business of leading an orchestra or a meeting

explanation.surface: A leader is no good at a business of leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is the metal Pb, not a leader: it carries electric current poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a poor transmitter of electricity, and directing a choir or orchestra is the business of a conductor.

clue.text: Ignored criminal taunted about death

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
criminal means wrongly arranged, so the letters of taunted are rearranged

parts.note: death is one's end

explanation.surface: A victim was ignored after a criminal taunted them about death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TAUNTED into UNATTED, which goes 'about' END.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unattended is left alone without care or supervision, so it has been ignored.

clue.text: Listless state university dons ruined sport

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the rearranged letters are worn around the other piece
ruined means the letters of sport are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: University lecturers have spoiled a sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb: U puts on the rearranged SPORT (STPOR), ending up inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, torpid condition, a listless state of near unconsciousness.

clue.text: Current name's position in town apparently

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for name, and in a down light the N of town is written beneath the other letters
the letters standing above that N in town are T, O and W

explanation.surface: A reflection on where one's name appears within a town.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name; in a down light, the N of TOWN is under TOW.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current beneath the surface flowing away from the shore.

clue.text: Gorge on a slice of cake (and then some) for starters

indicators.note: a slice of means just one letter, the first, is cut from cake
for starters says that slice is the opening letter of cake

parts.note: and then some, meaning and more besides, stands for some, and some means any, as in have you any money

explanation.surface: An invitation to stuff oneself on cake and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb about eating but it is the noun, a deep valley; the piece from 'on' goes last, after the cake's slice and the 'and then some' piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, steep-sided gorge cut by a river.

clue.text: One presumably unwilling to co-operate with the Marines in the main

indicators.note: with means the two pieces are combined, the second set inside the first

parts.note: someone refusing to co-operate is presumably no ally
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A description of a stubborn person who won't work with the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks naval to go with the Marines, but it means for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main is an idiom meaning generally or usually, a synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: Provincial social worker raising vegetables

indicators.note: raising means, in a down light, the first piece is held up on top of the second

parts.note: peas are vegetables
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A social worker in the provinces grows vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a caseworker but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rustic country person, so a provincial in the disparaging sense of an unsophisticated outsider.

clue.text: Shot indiscreet suspect

indicators.note: suspect means unreliable or questionable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless suspect is shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' describes fabric woven so its colour changes with the light, as in shot silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk shimmers in changing colours, and iridescent describes that same rainbow shimmer.

clue.text: Server's terminal connects to external part of network

indicators.note: terminal means the final letter of server is taken

parts.note: external means outer

explanation.surface: Computing jargon: a server's terminal is wired to the outer edge of a network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' and 'terminal' look like networking terms but simply give the last letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a device forwarding data between parts of a computer network.

clue.text: Go off scratching head after bee sting

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the letter

parts.note: the letter B sounds like bee

indicators.note: scratching head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: milk that goes off is said to turn

explanation.surface: A bee sting flares up and the victim scratches their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn is to give a smarting, stinging pain, as nettles or iodine do.

clue.text: Where one might write saying you are in lover's embrace

indicators.note: embrace means the lover's word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a beau is a lover or boyfriend

indicators.note: saying means the words are spoken, and you are sounds like the letters U R

parts.note: spoken aloud, the words you are sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: A romantic declaration made while wrapped in a lover's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' turns 'you are' into UR, text-speak letters that sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a writing desk with a sloping fold-down lid, a place to write letters.

clue.text: Number, no less, that can decide question or statement of uncertainty

definitions.text: Number, no less, that can decide

parts.note: um is the sound of a hesitant speaker

explanation.surface: A query whether a number can settle a matter, met with hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members needed for a meeting to make valid decisions.

clue.text: Girl showing cheek by lifting short short skirt

indicators.note: lifting means, in a down light, the letter holds the other piece up above it
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
by means times, as in 3 by 4, written X

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl hitching up her already short skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is an impudent, flirtatious young woman, a girl with plenty of cheek.

clue.text: Radiation screen cures man's disorder

indicators.note: disorder means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of cures and man, the apostrophe s being read as is

explanation.surface: A screening for radiation exposure supposedly cures a man's illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like an illness but signals that the letters of CURES MAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun cream blocks ultraviolet rays from the sun, so it is a screen against radiation.

clue.text: Aim for one dividing 175% of nothing

indicators.note: dividing means the letter splits the other piece in two

parts.note: one whole word for nothing, zero, plus three-quarters of another, none
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mathematical oddity: dividing by one a quantity that is 175% of zero.
explanation.walkthrough: The 175% is one whole word for nothing plus three-quarters of a second (NONE less its E); 'dividing' puts the I between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To zero in on a target is to focus on it closely, a phrasal synonym of aim for.

clue.text: Authorise objective whose conclusion should be accomplished

indicators.note: whose conclusion should be means the last letter is swapped for the following word

parts.note: an objective is an end or goal
accomplished means able or skilled

explanation.surface: Approving a goal on condition that its completion is achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion' is the last letter of END, the D that gives way to ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to give power or permission to do something, so it means to authorise.
